subject: English Language
text: Each of the students ___ a copy of the handbook.
explanation: Use singular verb with 'Each of the…' because the subject is treated as singular: 'Each ... has'. Rule: singular agreement.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the guests arrived, Lydia ___ the cake.
explanation: Use past perfect for an action completed before another past event: 'had baked' shows earlier completion than 'arrived'.

subject: English Language
text: His answer was full of ___; he avoided the truth.
explanation: Ambiguity fits because avoiding truth involves being unclear. Candour/clarity/precision mean openness or exactness.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is most appropriate for a formal letter of complaint?
options: I gotta tell you I'm angry about this.
You messed up my order — fix it now.
This is to notify you that I'm upset.
I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with your service.
explanation: Formal complaints use polite, complete phrasing: 'I am writing to express my dissatisfaction...' is suitably formal and conventional.

subject: English Language
text: Consider the sentence: my sister said, 'we will leave at ten.' Which version is correctly capitalised and punctuated?
options: My sister said, "We will leave at ten."
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Correct: capitalise first word inside quotes and place closing punctuation inside. Quotation marks require 'We' capitalised and final full stop inside.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following words has primary stress on the first syllable? (Tested words: pencil, about, because, arrive)
explanation: Two-syllable nouns like 'PEN-cil' have stress on the first syllable; 'about', 'because', 'arrive' have stress later.

subject: English Language
text: Which of these words ends with the /t/ sound?
explanation: The final consonant in 'fact' is /t/. 'Phase' ends /z/, 'face' ends /s/ (or /s/ with voiceless), 'fade' ends /d/ sound.

subject: English Language
text: Speaker A: "Could you close the window?" What is the function of this utterance?
explanation: 'Could you...' is a polite request asking someone to perform an action. It is not an apology, offer, or suggestion.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: Farmers harvest cassava every year.
options: Cassava is harvested by farmers every year.
Cassava are harvested by farmers every year.
Farmers are harvested cassava every year.
Cassava was harvested by farmers every year.
explanation: Present simple passive: plural noun 'Cassava' takes singular 'is' here as uncountable/mass; correct form: 'Cassava is harvested by farmers every year.'

subject: English Language
text: Amaka left her umbrella at Mr Bello's shop. She asked him to keep it until she returned. Why did Amaka ask Mr Bello to keep the umbrella?
options: Because she wanted him to sell it.
Because she wanted to borrow it from him.
Because she gave it to him as a present.
explanation: Inference: asking someone to keep an item 'until she returned' implies she intends to retrieve and use it later, not to sell, borrow, or gift it.

subject: English Language
text: Each of the committee members ____ responsible for a section.
explanation: With 'each' as a distributive subject, use a singular verb: 'each ... is'. This contrasts with plural verbs used with plural subjects.

subject: English Language
text: By next month, I ____ completed the project.
explanation: Future perfect uses 'will have' + past participle to show completion before a future time: 'will have completed'.

subject: English Language
text: Consider the sentence: "dr. awudu will speak at the conference." Which version is correctly capitalised and punctuated?
options: Dr. Awudu will speak at the conference.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
Doctor Awudu will speak at the conference.
explanation: Abbreviated title 'Dr.' requires a capital D and a period; names are capitalised: 'Dr. Awudu will speak...'.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following words has primary stress on the second syllable? (Tested words: control, country, device, teacher)
explanation: In 'deVICE' the primary stress falls on the second syllable, whereas 'CONtrol' and 'COUNtry' have first-syllable stress.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following words ends with the /d/ sound? (Tested words: bag, bake, base, bad)
explanation: Phonetically, 'bad' ends with the voiced alveolar stop /d/; 'bag' /g/, 'bake' /k/ and 'base' /s/ are different final sounds.

subject: English Language
text: Bukky is meticulous about arranging her books. What does 'meticulous' most nearly mean here?
explanation: 'Meticulous' means paying great attention to detail = careful. The other choices are antonyms or unrelated.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the sentence most appropriate for a job interview.
options: "I am eager to contribute my skills to your team."
"Hey, what's up? Can I get this job?"
"You people should hire me; I'm the best."
"Give me the chance and I'll show you."
explanation: Formal, polite register suits interviews: 'I am eager to contribute...' is professional. Others are informal or aggressive.

subject: English Language
text: Speaker: "Could you show me the way to the market?" What is the function of this utterance?
options: A request for information or help
explanation: The modal 'Could you...' is a polite request asking for directions or assistance, not an offer or refusal.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: "Olufemi will deliver the parcel tomorrow."
options: The parcel will deliver Olufemi tomorrow.
Olufemi will be delivered the parcel tomorrow.
The parcel will be delivered by Olufemi tomorrow.
The parcel was delivered by Olufemi tomorrow.
explanation: Passive: object becomes subject + 'will be' + past participle + 'by' agent: 'The parcel will be delivered by Olufemi.'

subject: English Language
text: When the rains started, the farmers hurried to the field. They wanted to ____ the seed before it washed away.
explanation: After 'wanted to' use the base infinitive: 'wanted to sow'. 'Sowed' or 'sowing' would be grammatically incorrect here.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the manager nor the employees ___ willing to work late.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer noun; 'employees' (plural) requires 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the meeting starts, I ___ the draft for the report.
explanation: The future perfect ('will have' + past participle) expresses an action finished before a future time: 'will have completed.'

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'She was discreet about the surprise,' what does 'discreet' most nearly mean?
explanation: 'Discreet' means careful and tactful in behaviour or speech; it does not mean loud or public.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is most appropriate for opening a formal email to a university professor?
options: Hey Prof, I need help with my paper.
Just checking if you got my essay.
Can you please look into my file?
I am writing to inquire about the status of my application.
explanation: A formal opening uses a complete polite phrase such as 'I am writing to inquire...' rather than informal greetings or short commands.

subject: English Language
text: Consider the sentence: 'dr. mmeh will chair the seminar on thursday.' Which version is correctly capitalised and punctuated?
options: Dr. Mmeh will chair the seminar on Thursday.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Titles and names take initial capitals and the abbreviation 'Dr.' has a full stop; days are capitalised: 'Dr. Mmeh ... Thursday.'

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following words has primary stress on the first syllable? Tested words: 'happy', 'discuss', 'computer', 'arrange'.
explanation: 'Happy' is stressed on the first syllable ('HAP-py'); 'discuss', 'computer', 'arrange' have primary stress later in the word.

subject: English Language
text: Which of these words ends with the /tʃ/ sound? Tested words: 'watch', 'glass', 'bag', 'save'.
explanation: The word 'watch' ends with the /tʃ/ (ch) sound; 'glass' ends /s/, 'bag' /g/, 'save' /v/.

subject: English Language
text: Speaker A: 'Could you hand me the stapler, please?' What is the function of this utterance?
explanation: The use of 'Could you... please?' signals a polite request for action, not an apology, warning or suggestion.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'Someone repaired the road yesterday.' Which is correct?
options: The road has been repaired yesterday.
explanation: Simple past passive uses 'was' + past participle: 'The road was repaired yesterday.' Other forms are ungrammatical or wrong tense.

subject: English Language
text: After the rehearsal, Nneka felt confident because she had ____ her lines.
explanation: With 'had' the past perfect requires the past participle form 'learned'. 'Had learned' = action completed before another past event.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ the announcement.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'students' (plural), so use 'were surprised'.

subject: English Language
text: By 6 p.m. tomorrow, I ____ this article.
explanation: Use future perfect 'will have finished' to show an action completed before a future time (by 6 p.m.).

subject: English Language
text: He spoke in a terse manner.
explanation: 'Terse' means brief and to the point, so 'using few words' is the closest meaning; other choices contradict brevity.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is most appropriate for a formal job application?
options: Hey, I need this job; I can start immediately.
Please accept my application for the advertised teaching position.
I'm sending my CV because I'm looking for work.
Can you give me this job? I have experience.
explanation: Option 2 uses polite, formal language and a clear statement of purpose appropriate for applications; others are informal or vague.

subject: English Language
text: Consider the sentence: mr. adejo will present 'the new plan' on monday. Which version is correctly capitalised and punctuated?
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
Mr. Adejo will present 'The New Plan' on Monday.
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Proper nouns and days are capitalised and titles in quotes are title-cased: 'Mr. Adejo', 'The New Plan', 'Monday' is correct punctuation and capitalisation.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following words has primary stress on the second syllable? (Tested words: banana, teacher, garden, market)
explanation: Banana is stressed on the second syllable (ba-NA-na). The other words carry primary stress on the first syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following words ends with the /d/ sound? (Tested words: cold, pack, paste, curb)
explanation: 'Cold' ends in the voiced consonant /d/ (pronounced /koʊld/). The others end with different consonant sounds (/k/, /st/, /b/).

subject: English Language
text: Speaker: "Would you mind closing the gate?" What is the primary function of this utterance?
explanation: Polite question form 'Would you mind...?' functions as a request asking someone to perform an action, not a command or offer.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'The committee will announce the results tomorrow.'
options: Tomorrow will be announced the results by the committee.
The results will announce the committee tomorrow.
The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The committee will be announced the results tomorrow.
explanation: Correct passive moves object to subject: 'The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.' preserves tense and agent placement.

subject: English Language
text: Tomiwa watered the seedlings at dawn. Why did he most likely do this?
options: To make them grow only at night
To add chemical fertiliser to the leaves
To stop them from producing flowers
To prevent them from wilting in the midday heat
explanation: Watering at dawn is commonly done to give plants moisture before heat; this prevents wilting—other options are implausible in context.

subject: English Language
text: Every one of the applicants ____ to submit a copy of their certificate.
explanation: With 'Every one of' the subject is singular, so the verb takes singular form: 'is required' is grammatically correct.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the concert begins, we ____ the tickets from the box office.
explanation: Future perfect expresses completion before a future point: 'will have collected' shows tickets obtained before the concert begins.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'Mojisola is frugal with her money,' what does 'frugal' most nearly mean?
explanation: 'Frugal' means being careful with spending or economical; it contrasts with 'wasteful' or 'generous'.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence is most appropriate to begin a formal complaint letter to a landlord?
options: Hey, you need to fix the leak now!
Can you sort out this leak when you have time?
Just letting you know the sink is faulty.
I am writing to report a persistent leak in flat 4B.
explanation: Formal letters use neutral, clear openings: 'I am writing to report...' is appropriately polite and specific for a complaint.

subject: English Language
text: Consider the sentence: "professor emeka said, 'the lecture starts on monday.'" Which version is correctly capitalised and punctuated?
options: Professor Emeka said, 'The lecture starts on Monday.'
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Titles and names, sentence-initial words and days are capitalised; the quoted sentence begins with a capital letter: full correct form shown in option 1.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable carries the primary stress in the word 'economy'?
explanation: The common pronunciation is e-CON-o-my, with primary stress on the second syllable; therefore 'second syllable' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Which of these words ends with the /ʃ/ sound? (Tested words: dish, dog, fade, bag)
explanation: The final sound of 'dish' is /ʃ/ (sh), while 'dog' ends /g/, 'fade' /d/, and 'bag' /g/; phonetic contrast identifies 'dish'.

subject: English Language
text: Speaker: "Could you tell me how to get to the post office?" What is the primary function of this utterance?
explanation: The speaker asks for directions, so the utterance's function is requesting information, not ordering or offering.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: "They will publish the novel next month." Which is correct?
options: The novel will be published next month.
The novel will publish next month.
The novel will have published next month.
The novel is published by them next month.
explanation: Future simple passive is formed with 'will be' + past participle: 'will be published' is correct; other options misuse voice or tense.

subject: English Language
text: After reading the safety bulletin, the crew took measures to avert an accident. What does 'avert' most nearly mean here?
explanation: 'Avert' means to prevent or avoid something bad from happening; context of safety measures confirms 'prevent'.
